notes: The Portugal-Berkeley call (official source: fct.pt/concursos/programa-portugal-berkeley-1) requires candidates, before applying, to 'identify and obtain agreement from a UC Berkeley faculty member who will act as supervisor during the stay', and names the UC Berkeley Center for Portuguese Studies (CPS) as the host institution that handles Visiting Student Researcher procedures. No fixed list of supervisors is published by FCT or UC Berkeley (any Berkeley faculty member in any field may act as host), so the professors recorded here are the leadership and Faculty Board of the CPS - the Berkeley unit that implements the programme under the FCT/CPS-Berkeley protocol and the closest official tie to this scholarship. Programme contacts published on the FCT page: fctberkeley@fct.pt (FCT), ricardo.pereira@flad.pt (FLAD), csp@berkeley.edu (CPS). CPS Executive Director Sydney Weaver (csp@berkeley.edu) is professional staff rather than faculty and is therefore not listed as a professor.

Programa RESTART (4th edition) is a Portuguese national FCT funding instrument: a competitive individual R&D project grant of up to EUR 50,000 for a maximum of 18 months, held by the beneficiary R&D unit (not a personal stipend). The applicant is the doctorate-holding researcher who runs their own project at their own host R&D unit or State laboratory; no supervising professor or academic programme is attached to the scheme, so supervisor enrichment is not applicable. Eligibility contact published on the FCT page: restart@fct.pt.

CLP Future Conservationist Awards are charitable, team-based conservation project grants (up to US$15,000, projects of 6-12 months) run by the Conservation Leadership Programme partnership of BirdLife International, Fauna & Flora and the Wildlife Conservation Society. Teams of at least three early-career conservationists (max five years' professional experience) who are nationals of the project country; support is delivered through the CLP global Alumni Network, training (Conservation Management & Leadership workshops) and mentorship - not through any university, department or academic supervisor. Direct webfetch of conservationleadershipprogramme.org repeatedly returned transport errors (likely bot protection); the programme details were confirmed from the official CLP domain content indexed in search (Future Conservationist Award page and 2027 Guidelines document). No supervising professor is attached to the award.

The Rufford Small Grants Programme is a charitable, staged field-work grant from the Rufford Foundation (1st RSG up to GBP 7,000; 2nd RSG up to GBP 8,000; Booster up to GBP 12,000; Completion up to GBP 18,000), funding fieldwork costs only, with rolling applications. Priority goes to early-career conservationists, including those undertaking an MSc or PhD, but the Foundation is not attached to any institution and requires no host university, supervisor or faculty; the applicant designs and runs their own small-scale or pilot nature conservation project. No supervising professor is attached to the grant.

The Whitley Awards (Whitley Fund for Nature) are annual conservation leadership awards worth GBP 50,000 in project funding over one year, given to nationals of the country in which they work to scale up proven grassroots, science-based conservation work. Applications require three applicant-nominated referees; winners receive communications/media support, peer learning and training, and eligibility for Continuation Funding and the Whitley Gold Award. No academic institution, degree programme or supervising professor is attached to the award, so supervisor enrichment is not applicable.

The Ibrahim Leadership Fellowships place three Fellows per year for 12 months in the executive offices of the African Development Bank (Abidjan), UN Economic Commission for Africa (Addis Ababa) or the International Trade Centre (Geneva), funded by the Mo Ibrahim Foundation with a stipend of $100,000. It is a professional work placement (research and policy design) requiring a Master's degree, not a degree-granting scholarship. The only mentorship published is from the head of the host organisation - quoted on the Foundation's page from Pamela Coke-Hamilton (Executive Director, ITC), Akinwumi Adesina (President, African Development Bank) and Claver Gatete (Under-Secretary-General and Executive Secretary, UN ECA). These are institutional/policy mentors, not academic supervising professors, and no university is involved, so no professor entries are recorded.

The Mandela Rhodes Scholarship is a Foundation postgraduate scholarship (one-year Honours or two-year Masters, fully funded) that may be taken at any of roughly 25 recognised South African institutions chosen by the applicant - including UCT, Wits, Stellenbosch, UKZN, Rhodes, Pretoria, UJ and others. The applicant applies separately to the university and the academic supervisor is arranged at that institution; the Mandela Rhodes Foundation publishes no supervising professor or faculty for the scholarship. The Foundation's leadership development programme uses an optional voluntary mentoring programme pairing scholars with programme alumni and sector-specific alumni advisors for group projects, but no names of these mentors/advisors are published on official pages, so no verified professor could be recorded. Official source: mandelarhodes.org/scholarship/apply.
